edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 8

source_text: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie, ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum. Meridies plena lux est et perfecta cognitio. Sponsa non vespere nec diluculo, sed in meridie pascua Verbi quaerit. Sine indicatione sponsi errat inter greges alienos — dogmata et sectas.
pass_a_gloss: Indicate to-me whom loves soul my, where you-may-pasture, where you-may-lie at-noon, lest to-wander I-may-begin after flocks of-companions your. Noon full light is and perfect knowledge...
pass_b_english: [[Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture, where you lie down at noon, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of your companions >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:7]]. Noon is full light and perfect knowledge. The Bride seeks the Word’s pastures not at evening or dawn but at noon. Without the Bridegroom’s showing she wanders among alien flocks — doctrines and sects.
